title: Integration Handoff Room
user: Small software agencies and fractional engineering teams that need clients to accept an API integration with executable examples, decisions, and ownership—not a pile of docs and email.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A small dev team has onboarding, design, API, and operational docs scattered across Notion, Drive, GitHub, and Slack and wants something that stays easy to maintain and sync.
API developers and QA need reusable valid, invalid, and localized request variants for debugging, regression, and team handoff; the request asks for persisted multi-payload request tabs.

recurrence: Documentation is scattered while the payloads needed to verify the integration live in personal tooling. The gap recurs at every client release and handoff.
current_workaround: Send Notion or Drive links, share Postman or Bruno collections, run screen-share acceptance calls, and reconstruct agreements when support begins.
incumbents_and_gap: Notion, Confluence, Postman, Bruno, and Stoplight manage docs or requests. None is a small agency-facing acceptance room binding a selected executable example, a decision, and a named client acknowledgement.
smallest_useful_product: Git-connected release room with sanitized request/response fixtures, acceptance checklist, client questions, versioned decisions, and signed-off handover export. It is not an API gateway, test runner, source-code host, or general wiki.
success_measure: In pilot projects, 80% of client integration questions are answered from the handoff room and post-handoff clarification hours decline by 30%.
monetization: Subscription — $79/month per agency for active client rooms; client reviewers are free.
constraints: Never store live secrets; automatically redact fixtures; repository OAuth has least privilege; provide export/delete controls; explain that acknowledgement is not a substitute for a contract.
why_distinct: It turns handoff into a verified client-facing artifact instead of trying to replace a docs platform or API client.
